title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. A camera system picked up plates and produced a hit on a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies, and deputies acted on that hit as though it settled who was in the car in front of them. The stop was made with weapons drawn, at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, before anyone confirmed the vehicle matched.

The failure sits at the handoff between the camera alert and the armed stop. Deputies could not read the plates on the car they had stopped, which is the one check that would have separated the alert from the vehicle, and the stop proceeded anyway. Only after the men were handcuffed did deputies recognise the wrong car and show them a picture of the stolen vehicle.

Catching this would have required reading the plate on the stopped car before escalating to a felony stop, or treating the camera hit as a lead to be verified rather than a fact to be enforced. It is not established whether the camera misread a plate or whether deputies acted on an alert that did not correspond to the car they stopped, and the men's account of the threat to shoot is their allegation. The sheriff's office has said supervisors will review body-worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed, which is a review, not a finding.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
Harris County sheriff's deputies in Cypress, Texas, mistook two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves on Aug. 3. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and one deputy threatened to shoot, according to the men. The deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies after flock cameras picked up plates, but they could not read the plates on the car they stopped.

After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car and showed them a picture of the stolen vehicle. The men were not charged. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office says supervisors will review body-worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
